title: Reliability guardrails: productization & squad readiness plan
body:
Purpose
This doc lays out a cross-functional, product-oriented approach to make Service Level Objectives (SLOs) a first-class part of feature delivery and team readiness. The focus is not just on defining SLOs but on creating repeatable guardrails, release gates, and roll-forward/rollback behaviors that squads can adopt with minimal friction.

Context and motivation
- Observed gap: features ship without clear SLI definitions or error budget considerations; operators react after customer impact.
- Goal: reduce outages by shifting reliability left (product + dev + SRE collaboration) and make SLOs an integrated release criterion.
- Scope: public-facing API routes, internal model-serving tier (inference), and streaming endpoints.

High-level goals (Q1 2026)
1) Standardize SLI definitions and template SLOs for the three target surface areas (API, model-serving, streaming).
2) Build a lightweight squad readiness checklist that becomes a gating criterion for canary and GA rollouts.
3) Create tooling + templates so product and engineering can publish an SLO bundle with each feature PR.
4) Pilot with 3 squads and measure change in error-budget burn and mean time to mitigation (MTTM).

Who does what (roles & responsibility)
- Squad Product Lead: defines user-impact intents & acceptable degradation windows.
- Squad Engineering Lead: implements instrumentation and release gating, owns rollout playbook.
- SRE Partner: validates SLI accuracy, advises on alert thresholds, owns escalations and global runbooks.
- Observability Team: builds dashboard templates, alert rule templates, and automated smoke checks.
- QA & E2E: owns synthetic tests that map to SLIs for canary stages.
- Release Engineering: integrates SLO gate into CI/CD (canary blocking) and plays coordination role for cross-squad rollouts.

SLO templates (examples squads should use as starting points)
1) Public API (text generation endpoints)
- SLI: 95th percentile request latency (server-side processing, excluding network) for 1-2k token requests.
- SLO: p95 latency \u003c= 650 ms, measured over 30d rolling window.
- Error budget policy: 10% monthly burn allows progressive rollout; if burn rate \u003e 25% for 3 consecutive days, halt canary and rollback unless mitigations are in place.

2) Model-serving (inference GPU pools/dedicated)
- SLI: tail memory OOM rate (OOMs per 1M requests) + KV cache hit ratio for prefix-heavy workloads.
- SLO: OOM rate \u003c 3 per 1M; cache hit ratio \u003e 70% for identified workloads.
- Error budget policy: immediate throttle to dedicated capacity if OOM trend rises; automated fallback to cached responses for non-critical calls.

3) Streaming (token-streaming or chunked responses)
- SLI: mean time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and end-to-end stream completeness (percent of sessions that finish without interruption).
- SLO: TTFB \u003c= 180 ms p50; completion rate \u003e 99.3% over 14d.

Squad readiness checklist (to be attached to feature PR and release ticket)
- Instrumentation: metrics emitted for the chosen SLI + tags (cluster, region, model-version).
- Dashboards: squad-specific dashboard created from template and linked in PR.
- Synthetic tests: canary suite with 2 customer-like scenarios (happy path + failure injection).
- Alerting: alert conditions and runbook link added to alert payload; runbook owner assigned.
- Rollout plan: % canary schedule, rollback conditions, and fallbacks (model variants/region routing).
- Cost/throughput assessment: expected tokens/sec and GPU footprint; if expected unit-cost \u003e 2x baseline, require SRE signoff.
- Compliance check: any data residency or key management requirements noted (Private deployment impact).

Release gating policy (how SLOs tie to CI/CD)
- Canary stage: must pass synthetic tests and show no >15% error-budget burn during a 48h window.
- Expanded canary: after 72h, monitor a 7d trend; if error budget burn rate \u003c threshold, proceed to GA.
- Emergency stop: automated cutover to fallback variant when alert "slo-critical" fires (configured in release-engineering).

Tooling & templates (deliverables for Q1)
- SLO Bundles: JSON/YAML template that squads attach to PRs (contains SLIs, SLOs, alerting, runbook links).
- Dashboard starter kit: Grafana/Lens dashboards with parameterized variables for service/model.
- Canary harness checklist: Jenkins/GitHub Actions workflow snippets that run synthetic tests and surface results in PR.
- On-call playbook snippets: short runbooks for common failures (high-latency, OOM, cache degradation).

Pilot plan (3 squads, 8 weeks each)
Week 0-1: onboarding workshop (SRE + Observability + product) — define intents per squad.
Week 2-3: instrumentation sprint — implement metrics and basic dashboard.
Week 4: synthetic test + canary harness integration.
Week 5-6: monitor canary, iterate thresholds, SRE validates readiness.
Week 7-8: GA roll, collect metrics for retrospective and ERB (error budget review).

Success metrics for pilot
- % of features with SLO bundles attached at PR merge (target 80%).
- Reduction in number of Sev2+ incidents attributed to feature rollouts (target -30% over quarter).
- Mean time to mitigation (MTTM) when error budget burns begin (target \u003c 45m for pilot squads).

Risks and mitigation
- Risk: squads treat SLOs as checkbox. Mitigation: require SRE validation and periodic audits; make SLO dashboard presence visible in team OKRs.
- Risk: noisy SLI signals. Mitigation: observability team provides query tuning clinic and retention guidance.
- Risk: rollout slows velocity. Mitigation: lightweight templates, automation to reduce manual steps; focus pilot on high-impact paths.

Open questions (for leadership and product)
- Which executive body will arbitrate cross-squad SLO tradeoffs when two services compete for the same error budget? (Proposed: Reliability Council, reps from SRE/Product/Platform).
- How do we handle experimental model versions that intentionally degrade some SLIs for cost savings? Need explicit product-level acceptance flows.

Next steps (next 30 days)
- Align on the three pilot squads and schedule workshops (owner: Aisha).
- Deliver SLO bundle template and dashboard starter kit (owner: Observability team).
- Create a JIRA epic for the pilot and link to this doc: JIRA-1234.

Appendix: quick checklist for PRs (copyable)
- [ ] SLO bundle attached (SLIs \u002b SLOs)
- [ ] Dashboard link present
- [ ] Canary synthetic tests added to workflow
- [ ] Runbook link + on-call owner assigned
- [ ] Release cadence and rollback criteria documented

Notes to self (work-in-progress)
- Add sample YAML SLO bundle snippet with placeholders for service, model-version, and canary schedule.
- Coordinate with product-hosted-api to add gen-api-specific instrumentation libraries.
